DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Diary Beside the Declaration

STS-HS11-L4-1400P-HSELA1112-HJD-MNA-01 • HS English 11-12 • Foundational U.S. Documents: Themes, Purposes, and Rhetorical Features
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Historical journals let a reader stand inside a moment instead of reading about it. Layla, Tarek, and Rania are pairing invented diary entries from a family who arrived from Beirut and Casablanca with the exact lines those readers met for the first time in English. A diary says I felt. The Declaration says we hold.
Which one persuades a stranger more, and what does each one want from its reader?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Layla doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Layla is doing, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say what she is making a record of. Speak in academic English.
2
What is Tarek holding?
Look at the picture. Explain what Tarek has in his hands, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say why one family record is shown this large. Speak in academic English.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what the teacher is doing, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say why an adult is welcoming people this way. Speak in academic English.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Explain what kind of room this is, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say why this kind of room was chosen for this work. Speak in academic English.
5
Tell me about the exhibit wall.
Look at the picture. Explain what is on the big wall, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say how the handwriting and the printed words speak to each other. Speak in academic English.
6
What is Rania wearing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Rania has on, justify it with evidence from the picture, and say what her clothing adds to the picture of this family record. Speak in academic English.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
